claim.claim-text: 2. The method of claim 1, wherein when the investigating fails to determine an acceptable fault diagnosis within the single-fault hypotheses tier further comprising: moving to double-fault tier consisting of all hypotheses with two faults in the overall production system; re-partitioning, by the computer processor, the plurality of production modules of the production system into two groups of the production modules, wherein each of the groups are formed to likely have a single fault; and storing in a memory any acceptable fault diagnosis and corresponding probability.
3. The method according to claim 2, wherein the dissecting step generates more than two tiers, and the partitioning and investigating steps operate for each of the generated tiers.
4. The method according to claim 1, wherein the probability or likelihood for each hypothesis is calculated using observation data from the production system.
6. The method of claim 5, further comprising iteratively repeating steps C, D, E and F until step F(2) is performed.
7. The method of claim 5, wherein the hypothesis space is partitioned into j tiers where each tier is defined as the collection of hypotheses assuming a total of χj faults in the system.

8. The method of claim 5, wherein the production system is partitioned into subsystems where each subsystem is likely to have at most one fault based on the current observation data from the production system.

9. The method of claim 5, wherein the production system is partitioned into subsystems where each subsystem is likely to have at most one fault based on the aggregate of all the observation data from the production system.

10. The method of claim 5, wherein steps C, D, E, and F iteratively repeat until at least one of the following conditions occur: the current tier reaches a predetermined tier; or a predetermined amount of time elapses.

11. The method of claim 5, wherein the complexity of the method is O(M2), wherein O( ) is the standard complexity notation which means “in the order of”, and wherein M2 means the computation complexity is in the order of M×M.
14. The method of claim 13, wherein the subsystems are single-fault subsystems.
15. The method of claim 13, wherein the probability for each hypothesis is calculated using observation data from the production system.
16. The method of claim 13, wherein the probability for each hypothesis that the hypothesis contains a fault is calculated at least in part by using a Bayesian rule.

17. The method of claim 13, wherein each hypothesis is represented as a bit vector containing M bits; where M is the number of components in the production system, and each component in the production system is represented in the bit vector by one bit indicating whether a component is considered faulty in the hypothesis.
19. The system of claim 18, wherein the hypothesis space is partitioned into j tiers where each tier χj is defined as the collection of hypotheses assuming a total of j faults in the system.

20. The system of claim 18, wherein the production system is partitioned into subsystems where each subsystem is likely to have at most one fault based on the current observation data from the production system.

21. The system of claim 18, wherein the overall complexity of the method performed is O(M2), wherein O( ) is the standard complexity notation which means “in the order of”, and wherein M2 means the computation complexity is in the order of M×M.

22. The system of claim 18, wherein each hypothesis is represented as a bit vector containing M bits; where M is the number of components in the production system, and each component in the production system is represented in the bit vector by one bit indicating whether a component is considered faulty in the hypothesis.
24. The system of claim 23, wherein the probability for each hypothesis that the hypothesis contains a fault is calculated at least in part by using a Bayesian equation.
